solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Garment our sister altered one's taken off

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so these letters are rearranged into a new order
taken off means removed, so the numeral for one is dropped from the letters before rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to work with
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nun's habit has been altered, and someone has removed their own article of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from OUR SISTER, leaving OURSSTER, then rearrange those eight letters to get TROUSERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are an item of clothing worn on the legs, so they are a kind of garment.

clue.text: Drunk pinching priest's hat

indicators.note: pinching means gripping, so the first word holds the next inside it

parts.note: a toper is a habitual drinker
P is an abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A drunk steals a priest's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinching suggests theft in the surface; here it means holding P inside TOPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is informal for a top hat, a tall formal piece of headwear.

clue.text: Running exercises restricted by speaking

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: orating is speaking formally
physical education, school exercise lessons

explanation.surface: Running and other exercise are limited because someone keeps talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is operating is working or functioning, the same sense as running.

clue.text: Son satisfied eating large fish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the abbreviation goes within the word for satisfied

parts.note: met as in satisfied a requirement
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes

explanation.surface: A contented son eats a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The smelt is a small silvery food fish, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Stunning mythical bird, Charles?

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
Charles is one example of a king, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A spectacular legendary bird belonging to someone named Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocking is informal for excellent or impressive, a slang synonym of stunning.

clue.text: Colonel's only protecting admiral

indicators.note: the outer words protect, that is hold inside them, the letters wanted

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A colonel is the only officer guarding a senior naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The military ranks in the surface pull towards a general knowledge answer, but the name is sitting in plain sight inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson, victor at Trafalgar, is the most famous British naval commander of that rank.

clue.text: Get in coach right away, please

indicators.note: right away means the letter for right goes away, removed from the coach

parts.note: to enter is to get in
to train is to coach

explanation.surface: Climb into the coach immediately, if you would be so kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Please looks like a polite add-on but is the verb; TRAIN loses R to give TAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain an audience is to amuse and delight them, so both verbs mean giving pleasure.

clue.text: Crack visible at first in part of shoe

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the sole is the underside of a shoe

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of visible

explanation.surface: A split appears in the bottom of a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack reads as a split in the sole; it is the verb, as in cracking a code.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or code is to work it out, a synonym for solve as a verb.

clue.text: In town, regularly pick up rubbish

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the two words
to sense is to pick up on or detect

explanation.surface: Council workers regularly collect the litter in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Pick up and rubbish evoke refuse collection; rubbish is really the word for talk that makes no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is informal for foolish or meaningless talk, which is exactly what nonsense is.

clue.text: Dignified demeanour before scene changes

parts.note: the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: the word scene changes, meaning its letters move into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor keeps a calm, dignified manner just before the scene changes on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence is the impressive bearing or poise a person shows, a synonym for a dignified manner.

clue.text: Scarf and cardigan ultimately makes you hot

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: last letter of the knitted garment

explanation.surface: Wearing a scarf and a cardigan will make you warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says hot as in warm from woollens; the answer uses the slang sense of hot for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for recently stolen goods that are risky to sell, so the words are interchangeable.

clue.text: Go round the bend from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: round the bend and bats both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Driving around a bend in the road while heading north from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Round the bend is not about roads but slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is an attempt, as in have a go, and a stab is likewise an informal try.

clue.text: European cross by a court's demand

parts.note: standard abbreviation for European
a cross is the letter X in shape
taken as written
the usual abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: An angry European, standing by a court, makes a demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to insist on and obtain something, such as payment, so it is a verb meaning demand.

clue.text: Obstruct playwright heading off with free nuts

indicators.note: the playwright's heading, his first letter, comes off

parts.note: Harold Pinter, the English dramatist

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of free go wild and are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An unhinged playwright, free of all restraint, gets in people's way.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Pinter loses his P to give INTER; FREE is rearranged to FERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to get in the way of something, a direct synonym of obstruct as a verb.

clue.text: Turn back if gang's shooting

indicators.note: to turn back is to face the other way, so the short word is read right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is a criminal gang, as in a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: Run away if the gang starts opening fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing a gun is shooting it; both nouns name the discharge of weapons.

clue.text: Protection from cur's inane barking

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Guarding against a mongrel's pointless yapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking fits the dog perfectly in the surface, but it is British slang for crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance is cover that safeguards against loss or damage, so it is a form of protection.

clue.text: Birds following black dogs

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the birds are placed behind the colour

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
eagles are large birds of prey

explanation.surface: Birds of prey trail behind some black hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Beagles are a breed of small hunting hound, so they are examples of the animal named.

clue.text: Around middle of seminar, Glen isn't unfortunately paying attention

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the single middle letter
things that go unfortunately go wrong, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, the only one used here

parts.note: central letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Halfway through the seminar, sadly, Glen is not concentrating.
explanation.walkthrough: GLEN ISNT rearranges to LISTENNG, which goes around I from the centre of seminar.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening means giving attention to what is said, so it substitutes for paying attention.

clue.text: Dealing with worker left in rear of building

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of building

explanation.surface: Coping with an employee left behind at the back of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Handling a problem means managing or coping with it, a synonym for dealing with.

clue.text: Revered American golf course

parts.note: august means venerable and highly respected
standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A venerated American golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one description of a famous course; in fact the first two words build the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta National in Georgia is the golf course that hosts the Masters tournament each year.

clue.text: Salary wife's missed for a long time

indicators.note: something missed is left out, so the letter for wife is not included

parts.note: wages are pay
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: The husband's pay has not been noticed by his wife for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal idiom for a very lengthy period, as in waiting for ages.

clue.text: Conclusion bleak, possibly, about Northern Ireland

indicators.note: about means around, so the first item surrounds the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: a bleak is a small freshwater fish, so 'possibly' marks it as one example
standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The outlook for Northern Ireland is a bleak conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bleak looks like an adjective about the future, but here it is the noun for a small European river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is the end of something, a direct synonym for a conclusion.

clue.text: Most plump initially for a time trial

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of for
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: The heaviest cyclist starts first in a time trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Time trial looks like one cycling term but splits into T and TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Fattest is the superlative of fat, matching most plump as a superlative adjective.

clue.text: Scare female properly

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
right as in done properly

explanation.surface: Frighten a woman properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Scare looks like a verb in the surface, but the answer is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden shock of fear, the same as a scare used as a noun.

clue.text: Cleaner put off by grand hospital department

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
G is short for grand, a thousand
ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A cleaner is discouraged by the size of a big hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hospital cleaner; the definition is the substance, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a chemical substance for washing, so it is a cleaner in the sense of a cleaning agent.

clue.text: Swiss archer's orders

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to William Tell, the legendary Swiss bowman

explanation.surface: The commands given by a Swiss bowman.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell shot an apple off his son's head; the possessive gives the name with an S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tells as a verb means instructs or commands, and Tell's is the archer's possessive.

clue.text: Free limb almost trapped in vehicle

indicators.note: something trapped in a thing is held inside it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the limb is dropped

parts.note: a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Freeing a limb that has been nearly trapped inside a crashed vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear can be a verb meaning to free or acquit, as when someone is cleared of a charge.

clue.text: Short farm animal twice accepted drink

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the animal loses its last letter

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal
A is an abbreviation for accepted
the shortened animal is used two times

explanation.surface: A small farm animal twice accepted a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Short applies to the animal before it is doubled; A for accepted is a dictionary abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot beverage made from cacao powder, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Jersey, perhaps, is put down

parts.note: taken as written
to land a plane is to put it down

explanation.surface: A jumper is perhaps laid down on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the woollen garment, a jumper; here it is the Channel Island, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands off the coast of France, an example of an island.

clue.text: Arriving at emergency room flipping throbbing

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for emergency room
aching means throbbing with pain

explanation.surface: Turning up at A&E with a throbbing pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping in the surface sounds like a mild curse; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a place means getting to it, so it can replace arriving at in a sentence.

clue.text: Finally standing next to snake, Edward breathed hard

indicators.note: next to means placed alongside, so the pieces simply sit side by side
finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: last letter of standing
an asp is a venomous snake
Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward stood next to a snake and panted with fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to catch one's breath sharply, so gasped matches breathed hard as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Hearing sound, honest!

indicators.note: hearing a word rather than reading it means only its sound counts

parts.note: a sound is a narrow channel of sea, also called a strait

explanation.surface: Someone who heard a noise swears they are telling the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound reads as a noise; it is the noun for a sea channel, such as Plymouth Sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is an informal word for truthful and frank, as in a straight answer.
